title: Working system, reproducible evidence
narration: This is KeyGuard for DevForge Track Four. This narrated walkthrough uses actual recorded adapter and test output. The source, run scripts and evidence are available in the repository. The system uses real post quantum cryptography, not mocked signatures or a dataset classifier. Runtime decisions use registered identities, current policy and cryptographic verification.

title: Owner access and scenario isolation
narration: The real process per request adapter initializes a scenario, allows its owner to read and denies access after revocation. A second trusted setup replaces scenario tables in one transaction. Invalid replacement rolls back. Production initialization remains separate and refuses to overwrite an authority. Expected policy errors return structured JSON without pretending the process crashed.

title: Real protected reads
narration: Protected reads use real M L KEM seven sixty eight encapsulation. The proof is the exact organizer specified HMAC over the challenge concatenated with stored content. An independent Python implementation generated sixteen keys, decapsulated the actual Linux adapter responses and recomputed the proofs. Signature verification also passes two hundred twenty five pinned independent vectors.

title: Signed rotation and recovery
narration: Network commands bind the authority, destination audience, actor, key fingerprint, epoch, nonce, expiry and operation. Rotation verifies possession of the replacement key and commits the cutoff atomically. In flight transfers continue only during the old key's valid grace period. Two distinct custodians approve loss recovery, and stale approvers or competing proposals fail.

title: Independent nodes, bounded stale access
narration: Each node keeps an encrypted cache and signed policy chain. A sync needs the replicator credential and a signature from the node's own key, so a stolen credential cannot export. Across one hundred revocations, a stolen key stops working on every node within about one second. Each revoke reports when it holds everywhere. Partitioned nodes expire closed.

title: Crash safety and audit availability
narration: The suite actually kills a process during an uncommitted rotation and checks recovery. Authentication, effects and signed audit records share a transaction. Forged requests now update bounded minute counters instead of filling the signed log. Reaching the normal audit budget cannot block revocation or recovery. Physical disk failure remains a real limit to durable commits.

title: Backups and signed history
narration: File contents and identity backups are encrypted. Signed SHA three eighty four audit chains preserve record boundaries and correlation history. A trusted checkpoint detects an older restored backup. Cold startup verifies a signed saved checkpoint and checks only newer links; full exported history can be checked independently. Master keys are beside the database, so encryption protects database only leaks, not an entire compromised host.

title: Encrypted client delivery
narration: The recipient signs a one use ephemeral key offer bound to both peers. The sender encapsulates, derives a transcript bound key and encrypts locally. The relay stores ciphertext. Reordered and duplicate chunks are handled, conflicting or modified chunks fail, and incomplete messages expire. Real CLI processes transfer a file and acknowledge it. Session resumption is deliberately unsupported.

title: Detection beyond the practice set
narration: Both holdouts use separate reference and evaluation windows, and their scores are unchanged. On the organizer practice set, all five labelled findings alert, with no false alerts. Credential hopping across identities is detected. Labels only enter scoring. Synthetic accuracy is not a production guarantee.

title: Input diversity and realistic limits
narration: Input accepts timezone offsets and fractional seconds. A malformed or conflicting record is quarantined, not fatal. Unknown outcomes on role changes fail closed. One identity with a hundred thousand unusual edges is analysed in about a second. Benign three-edge fan-out can still alert, and hops more than thirty minutes apart are missed.
